record_scope_reconstruction: The through-road connecting Uzbekistan proper at Rishtan to the Sokh enclave traverses Kyrgyzstan and uses two separate road posts, Kaytpas and Otukchu. Passenger restoration excludes freight permission.

source_checks.finding: Russian full text names both Kaytpas and Otukchu, opened on 1 April 2021 for people and passenger vehicles; freight was not yet permitted. It explicitly notes disputed 2019 reopening reporting.
Names the Rishtan customs checkpoint and 19-km route, but does not locate both gates numerically.
Full history independently inspected: motor-road border control at the same coordinates since 2014, predating the 2019 dispute and 2021 reopening.
Current named Rishton node matched to the original 2021 article’s customs checkpoint and longstanding road-control node.

sites.name: Rishtan–Kaytpas road checkpoint, Uzbek side
sites.coordinate_method: Fresh OSM API XML node coordinates
sites.precision: Approximate crossing area, about 100 m; not the historical barrier footprint
sites.evidence_note: Explicit Rishton border_control node on the road south from Rishtan into Kyrgyzstan. Adjacent Kyrgyz node is currently labelled Kyrgyz-Kyshtak; original 2017 reports explicitly pair Rishtan with Kaytpas. The official indexed Kaytpas coordinate lies far away and is not adopted. Full node history shows the same road-control position since May 2014. The April 2021 Kun.uz reopening article explicitly identifies the Rishtan customs checkpoint on the Rishtan–Sokh route, while Azattyk names both Kaytpas and Otukchu. Only this Rishtan/Kaytpas end is located.
